utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. Could the registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-95-11-PT, the Prosecutor versus Milan Martic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: May we have the appearances, for the Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Alex Whiting for the Prosecution, along with Ms. Nisha Valabhji on my right, and Ms. Lakshmie Walpita on my left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: Thank you. And from the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I'm attorney-at-law Predrag Milovancevic, defence counsel for the accused Milan Martic. Together with me is the defence assistant, Mr. Vuk Sekulic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Martic, can you understand the proceedings in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. I am going to begin this Status Conference today referring myself to a very important item, which is the motions that are presented by the Prosecution for joinder of the cases of the Prosecutor versus Mr. Martic and the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic and the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj. This joinder motion, as you may know, have been assigned to a specially appointed Bench of this Tribunal. Due to the pending status of the joinder motion in this case, the Chamber has not rendered so far the decisions for motions under 92 bis and 94 bis presented. However, the Chamber understands the concerns of the party in this regard and will issue, try to issue the decision as an early as possible moment. I know that for you, Mr. Martic, the situation may change a lot, depending on your case being joined with another case or if you remain to be in your case yourself alone. So we know very much the implication of that, the problem that that means, because if you are remaining alone with your case, it may start, hopefully, perhaps at the end of this year, December; at the most, January. And if it is joined with the other cases I had mentioned, it may last still for a longer time. I know you are in a situation of detention which is not agreeable for you, it's not a pleasure for you to be there, I suppose, I know. And then we know the importance of deciding as soon as possible. So it's not for me to decide, but I want you to know what is the situation on the matter. Another point that has been mentioned yesterday, and it has been pointed out to me, is the situation of the translation into B/C/S of the report of the military analyst, Mr. Theunens. Could you please, representative of the Prosecution, Mr. Whiting, tell me what is the situation of this translation that has been already asked for and granted and not so far completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Actually, in fact, Your Honour, after the 65 ter conference yesterday, where the issue came up for the first time, we checked, and in fact the translation was completed, and it was disclosed to the Defence in mid-August, but it was placed on the EDS system. And a letter dated 11 August 2005 was sent to Defence counsel in this case, with a list of disclosure, including the B/C/S version of that expert report. So it was -- the bottom line is that this report was in fact disclosed in B/C/S more than a month ago. If I might, Your Honour, and I don't want to trouble the Court, but it's in the interest of perhaps saving Court time in the future, I would suggest that if these -- if there are questions about disclosure in the future, perhaps Defence counsel could make contact directly with the Prosecution and ask first before taking Court time with the matter, either in a 65 ter conference or in a Status Conference. Because often times, the matter can be resolved very expeditiously if we are contacted directly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: You heard, Mr. Milovancevic. I suppose you have already got to know the translation that has been mentioned of this part, Mr. Theunens. You have got it or you haven't?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this time, Your Honour, I'm unable to give you a definite answer. It is true that we received a large amount of material from the Prosecution. This involves thousands and thousands of pages of written material. Occasionally, delivery of such large amount of material to us can present a problem, because it is sent via express mail to our office, and occasionally, the same material is sent electronically. We will verify this fact and we will get back to the Prosecution immediately after that. We certainly don't want to raise issues if there's no need to do that. We brought this to the attention of the Prosecution because we could not find the translation, and I'm very happy to hear now that the translation has been provided. We will verify this and inform all parties. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: I expect you to revise those documents that had been sent to you and disclosed to you, and in case you didn't find easily these translations to which we are referring now, you have heard that the Prosecution -- the representative of the Prosecution has said and you can address himself directly so as to help you to find out. Another point which I would like to address is the agreed facts. In the previous Status Conference, I said to the parties that it would be interesting to work on those agreed facts in this case. However, I have been informed that there has been very little progress on this subject. And after the Status Conference we had in May, may I ask the parties to address me in this regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. There are some facts that have been agreed, and they were attached to the Defence pre-trial brief, and the Prosecution acknowledged in its 2 November 2004 submission that these were -- these agreed facts in fact represented the facts that have been agreed upon. But of course Your Honour is asking about progress that has been made since that date. I regret to say that there has been no progress, and from the perspective of the Prosecution, while we would like Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to have more agreed facts and have more progress on this issue, we're not very hopeful, given the positions of the parties, that that in fact can be accomplished. A lot of work went into reaching the facts that have already been agreed, which, to be frank, are not very substantial. And it is simply a reflection of the differences in the parties and the fact that the Defence has taken a certain approach on challenging this case that we do not believe it's likely that we will achieve further agreement. The Defence yesterday also indicated at the Status Conference that they have been unable, for various reasons, to do much additional work on the case, and indicated, as I understood, that they were not in a position to pursue agreed facts any further because they had been unable to work on the case. Perhaps that's something that can be addressed by Defence counsel. Having said that we are not very hopeful about achieving further agreement, we're always happy to sit down one more time with the Defence to see if there are areas perhaps where there's been change or there's been movement, modification in positions which would allow for agreement between the parties. But we may have reached the point where simply hoping for further agreement between the parties is not going to achieve, in fact, that agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: Even if the Defence takes an extra effort to try to reach some agreed facts?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I would welcome, I really would welcome any extra effort from the Defence, and we would be receptive and we would take the first opportunity to meet. And we have continuously in this case - and I think the record will reflect this - we have urged the Defence counsel in this case to make contact with us when they are in The Hague, to come and meet with us to discuss these matters. That invitation has not generally been accepted. So if the Defence is prepared now to take a fresh look at these issues and to consider further agreed facts, we would be happy to do that. It's in our interest and everybody's interest to reach agreement on everything that we can. And we're certainly willing to try to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Whiting. I am sure that agreeing on facts could be helpful and a good result for both parties. So please, Mr. Milovancevic, can you explain to the Court what is the matter with this point in concrete? Are you ready to restart to gain the question relating with the Prosecutor about finding facts on which you could agree?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm pleased that Mr. Whiting said that as far as the agreed facts are concerned, we covered quite a lot. Out of 45 proposed facts, we agreed on over 30 facts. This work on agreed facts is an ongoing process, and it depends on the efforts invested by both sides. Occasionally, the sides fail to understand the position of the other side, which leads to a delay in the process. It is in the interest of the Defence to reduce the length of the proceedings, not to lengthen them. In order for you, Your Honour, to understand the position of the Defence, I need to tell you that the OTP motions of the 19th of July and 17th of August, 2005 are the motions where the OTP wanted to vary the list of witnesses under Rule 65 ter, as well as the list of exhibits. Based on the work of their investigators conducted in 2004 and in 2005, there is a list of over 900 exhibits that ought to be admitted, and also a proposed number of new witnesses that should also be taken into account under Rule 65 ter. In order for the Defence to analyse this material, and this is an entirely new material, this material that came with the pre-trial brief of the OTP. After we analyse this material, we will be able to go over all outstanding issues with the Prosecution and perhaps we will be able to get something else done, to have some progress in that matter. In addition to the two motions of the OTP that I mentioned, there is also a motion of Defence, dated the 18th of March, 2005. In June of last year, the Defence applied to the Registry, asking for new funds in order to study the material submitted with the pre-trial brief. As I told you, this includes thousands and thousands of pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, not to confound subjects. So now we are dealing with the possibility of finding more facts on which parties can agree. May I understand that when you say that you go through the 900 new exhibits, you'll be in a position, and you are offering to the Prosecution the possibility of meeting again for trying to find new agreed facts? I have to remind you that it's not only from the Prosecution to suggest and to point out what facts could be agreed on, but also you can have the initiative in some matter, because it's beneficial for both parties. So should I understand when you say that you haven't been able to go through the 900 new exhibits, that afterwards you would be ready to start again having communications with the Prosecution for trying to find new facts on which to agree?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we will definitely get in touch with the Prosecution again. It is in our interest. We can contact them once we have studied the material. I would like to remind you once again that the list of witnesses given in the motion of the 19th of July, 2005, we received that two months ago. And this list of exhibits was something that we received just a month ago, on the 17th of August. And this involves 719 exhibits, not 900 exhibits. We received this electronically. We need to print this out and to go over this material. Once we do that, we will contact the Prosecution, especially since we already have some ready proposals concerning agreed facts. But we would like to put it all together and then have one position regarding the agreed facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: So I understand you haven't yet started having that structured in the form which you have received it. How long do you think it's going to take you to get knowledge of these 719 new exhibits? Because of the witnesses, I am not sure but I believe there are only five more new witnesses. So I understand that for the exhibits it may be a problem for you to get to know well about them. Please, can you tell me when you think you'll be through this work?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You've asked me something that is very difficult to answer, Your Honour. After we received this motion of the Prosecution dated the 17th of August -- or rather, we received it on the 25th of August, and we're about to print it now, because we Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. received it electronically and our technical capabilities are such that we were unable to print this earlier. We should be able to do this soon. Some exhibits have several pages, so this amount of exhibits could amount to thousands and thousands of pages. However, this is nothing new for the Defence. We are flooded with new material continuously, and we will try to study this as quickly as possible, and we'll contact the Prosecution immediately after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: What means "as quickly as possible"? One more month? Five weeks?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, when we received the OTP motion, with it came only the names of -- or the titles of the decisions and exhibits, with a summary, but not the documents in their entirety. Therefore, it is very difficult for me to give you an assessment, and I do not wish to mislead you. At any rate, we will proceed as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: So you cannot give us a concrete date at which you'll be through with that? Well, I hope -- more than hope, I expect you to be as quick as possible, and I will ask about that even before the next Status Conference, if ever we have one. I have to refer now to a matter which you had started to mention also, which is your allegation about the financial difficulties you find, that you believe is the most important issue in the preparation of this case. There is a motion for additional legal aid funds that you had filed lately in March 2005. But in the meantime of the resolution for that -- I hope the Chamber will render the decision as soon as possible. But in the meantime, I have to remind you the number of funds you had already received from the Registry. Perhaps it may help your memory if I tell you that, excluding the payment that was made for the previous Defence team, you had already been granted $271.209.43. May I remind you also that your case is ranked as level two, and those cases receive -- they are supposed to receive 2.100 counsel hours to prepare and 3.000 support staff hours. In level three, the case are supposed to receive 2.800 hours for the chief defence, and 4.000 hours for support staff. Then your case, which has been qualified level two, nevertheless had received more money than the level two, as average, receive. So far, you had been paid for 2.620 hours of prime time, if I may say, and 3.560 hours for staff support, for support staff. So I have to remind you that this Tribunal is not in a position that could allow it to allot unlimited resource to any Defence team. So please remember that and have that into your consideration, because it's not likely that you are going to get more money. Do you have anything to say around this matter, Mr. Milovancevic, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave, Your Honour, I would like to explain only the following: It is evident that the Martic case is a level two case. He has been provided with these funds because he is indigent. Every bill that was sent to the Registry was checked beforehand by the Registry. What is being held against us is the fact that we use these funds to study Prosecution material. That is the only purpose for which we use the funds so far, and this is in accordance with the discovery rules. On the other hand, the Defence team has not had any funds since March 2004, and the two motions that I mentioned before show that the Prosecution has continued its investigation since May last year, and that is what they stated two times last year and two times this year, all the way up to June 2005. So this is the Prosecution case. It's not defined by the Defence. If the Registry concluded that the accused Martic is indigent, I don't know how the Defence team can be expected to work without any funds for 17 months and to prepare the case successfully. At the 65 ter meeting yesterday, we were told that on the 12th of September, the request for provisional release was refused because the proper terms and conditions were not met. On the 14th of September, two days after that, we received the information that you repeated today, that this Chamber believes that this is a level two case. That means that the Prosecution continued its investigation for 16 months. Our hands are tied. We do not have funds. And at this point in time, the Prosecution wants to have trial joinder with level three cases. Martic has command responsibility involved, 19 counts, at that. And the other accused have only five counts. So obviously the decisions of different Trial Chambers are different when deciding on what level a case will be. What I've been saying, time and again, is that for 17 months we have been without any funds, and this drastically thwarts the interests of the accused and also the interests of justice, because this is very bad for the Tribunal too. And this is a problem that I face, and this is the fifth time and the fifth Status Conference when I appeal to have this redressed. Your Honour, it is impossible for us to file a motion for additional funds, which can be well-founded or not, I'm not pre-judging anything, but the accused is in detention for nine months and then the Registry keeps this and then they do not deal with it for nine months. Then again we submit a motion. It can be founded or unfounded, but realistically speaking it has to be founded, because we do not have any funds. So another six months were used. We do not have anything to do with defining the billing hours of lawyers or the amounts that will be charged for that. I engage in proper defence work and I'm indicating to the Trial Chamber that the situation we face now is an untenable one. That is the problem that we face.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: Not to mix the question of funding with the possibility of the joinder of the case with other cases in this Tribunal, what I had told you is that you had received these amounts of money and you had to review if these amounts of money exactly means the payment for the hours that you had been granted. If this is the case, you have to manage to do whatever is expected from you with the money you have received. So check about the money you have received and how many hours mean this amount of money of the work. And in case you haven't received as much money as the hours which have been granted to your case, even considering that your case has been granted more hours than the average time granted to level two cases, and then try to limit yourself to this. Because it's no use to tell me or to tell -- that you haven't got money Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. since a concrete date in the past. What you have to do is to calculate if the money you have received accounts for the amount of hours that you have been granted in this case. So please be serious about that. And in case this amount of money you haven't got completely paid, to be paid to you, you may ask for that to the Registrar. But otherwise, you have to know what you have done with your money according to the time that has been granted to you. Well, is there anything else the parties would like to tell me just now? Yes, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, Your Honour, this is a situation that is outside the powers of the Defence. Assigning cases a particular level is something that develops. First it was a level one case, then it turned into a level two case. The indictment against Martic was changed twice. Then there was a joinder of cases proposed. The fact that we did have funds assigned to us additionally shows that this is not a run-of-the-mill, level two case. But it also goes above level three. As Defence counsel, I cannot understand the situation in which the Trial Chamber bears in mind what the Defence counsel earn and do not pay attention to the fact that the accused is indigent. I see it the other way around. As Defence attorney, I supported every one of my bills with a list of the documents submitted by the Prosecution that were studied, and I gave the actual hours and minutes used for that, quite literally. The Registry approved each and every one of these bills. So for me, there is nothing controversial there. Quite simply, the Prosecution submits material to us. What is the Trial Chamber telling us now? This is the way I understand it, but please correct me if I'm wrong, Your Honour. We are told: You should have reallocated the funds you got. You should not have studied some of the materials that you did study, but you should have kept the money in order to study these additional materials that you received. That's not the way we can operate, Your Honour. With the approval of the Trial Chamber, we were given certain material through discovery, and each and every hour and minute was justified and approved by the Registry. But that was a long time ago, five Status Conferences ago, on the 17th of March, we remained without funds. I understand the need to economise and to be careful with the allocation of funds, but if the Registry does not have the funds to pay for the Defence of an accused person, we are not talking about five lawyers in Belgrade working free of charge now in order to keep this case alive. Now you have been presenting figures in a public session as to the funds that were used in total. I'm not hurt by that, although this is not the most decent thing to do. But the accused is in detention. The investigators do not have proper funds for their work, and what we are being told is: We don't care about this. You are there as Defence. And with this situation, this is only a semblance of trial readiness. Because the Defence is already greatly delayed. Please bear that in mind. We're not talking about the earnings of Defence attorneys.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: Well, I insist that you have to take care in how you allocate the money you had received for the purposes that it was received. So you had received more than the average, and perhaps it accounts for the difficulty that has been found, especially in your case. So I can't add anything else. Only I keep my reminder to you. Is there any other matter that you would like to put forward to the Chamber now?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, not from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: Well, in this case, I'll go and -- Mr. Martic, please, I believe that you don't have any trouble with your health.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Even if I did have problems, I wouldn't discuss it. Thank God, I'm fine. But I would like to ask you something, as a human being, with your permission, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Today is exactly three years and four months, or rather, 1.220 days that I've been here. I hear the same story all the time; when the trial will start, nobody knows. As for funds for my Defence, you are dealing with this in a wondrous way. No funds, no funds. And indeed, I'm going to set a record in waiting in prison, in detention. Today it is exactly three years and four months. Will I definitely get the right kind of Defence? My rights to a Defence are being denied in this way. There is no need to remind you that many of these witnesses are not accessible, and they are kilometres and kilometres away from my lawyers, and all of this means that there are expenses involved. But obviously no one has any understanding here. They only have understanding if it works to my detriment. As far as I can see here, there is constant pressure in terms of agreed facts or agreed positions, or whatever. This is an inversion of logic. I am innocent. That is what I assert, 100 per cent. But I'm still in detention. There is no trial, obviously, and no one knows when it will start. But if things continue this way, I will truly set a record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: First of all, the subject of -- you may sit down. The subject of your health is something that you don't hide to the Tribunal, because it's something we have to care for. So that is the first explanation I have to give to your words. Secondly, I agree with you, it's extremely unhappy that your case hasn't yet been started. And you may be sure that this Court is very preoccupied and concerned about how soon it could be started. It's unfortunately not for this Chamber, this particular Chamber, to resolve the situation, because it has to be solved previously the case about the possible joinder with the other two cases I had mentioned before. But you may be completely sure that you are not denied any possibility to express yourself and to take care of your Defence. So even if we realise that it's not perfect, the fact that you've had to wait for such a long time for your case to be heard, nevertheless it's something that we are caring, and caring to much. Be sure of that. Do you have any special complaints about the condition in which your detention is being done?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The conditions? No. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: You don't have problems, either to communicate with your lawyers or to have any -- what you need for this preparation of your Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the umpteenth time, let me repeat that I don't have any problem with the lawyers. They have a problem because they haven't got funds for their defence, and that's the problem. But this way -- yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: It is understood. And we take care of that, that you may know. Well, I hope that would be the last Status Conference for this case. It's not in my power to decide that. I think the next Status Conference, there hasn't been any special change for that, it will be held around mid-January, around mid-January. And if there is no other subject to be brought about, I have to conclude this meeting, not without expressing my thanks to the parties and to the Registry and to the interpreters. This Status Conference is closed, and we are adjourned.
